scope: Proposition 7.4 (Controlled pure lifts) of the manuscript “A high-arity counterexample to Pixton completeness in Chow” (preprints/A-high-arity-counterexample-to-Pixton-completeness-in-Chow-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 053 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 e52ae0e71ab4c7b5), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 49-50. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every stable heavy type (h, B) one can choose a symmetric class Gh,B ∈ A2(Xh,B(3)) with the following properties. (i) Over the smooth heavy base, Gh,B is exactly the pullback of ∆pure C by the coarse-position map. (ii) Pull a raw cubic F0, or one of these chosen pure lifts G, from any ancestor chart to a compact descendant cut chart. Its operation is a sum of the chosen pure lifts at the relevant descendant vertices, with all three labels assigned to that vertex, together with pair-times- singleton operations and a residual cubic operation. (iii) The singleton operations in (ii), and all their further pullbacks through cuts and light forgetting, are controlled as follows. Over fixed smooth core data their restrictions lie componentwise in the span of the unit, the canonical class, and the flag points. On any smooth test family the same statement holds modulo classes supported over positive base codimension. (iv) On the current smooth-core open the residual operation in (ii) is a finite sum of classes containing a pulled base divisor factor. The base divisor may come from the current heavy base or from a compact ancestor base. Consequently its pullback to every smooth test family is zero operationally after removing a positive-codimension subset of that test base. 49 All expansions preserve the color multiset. They may always use one and the same chosen G and centering at a given current vertex, regardless of which ancestor supplied the operation.
